summary: Turn 6. The Candidate from the previous turn (42418323715d4acdb3d131c86e9bb370, the handleCommit nil-lb dereference) is now resolved as explained by source investigation rather than escalated. Sourced reasoning: the branch at epaxos/epaxos.go:1092 that dereferences inst.lb.clientProposals requires commit.Replica == r.Id, and the row owner is the only creator of entries in its own row — handlePropose allocates into r.crtInstance[r.Id] (epaxos/epaxos.go:724-749) and startPhase1 installs InstanceSpace[replica][instance] together with a fresh LeaderBookkeeping before bcastPreAccept (epaxos/epaxos.go:751-779). Every other path that can produce a NOOP Commit for row R goes through a recovery leader's startPhase1(preply.Replica, ...) (epaxos/epaxos.go:1307-1312), which only recovers instances that already existed, and an (R,i) instance can only originate from R's own proposal. So in a crash-free execution the receiver's own-row entry always has non-nil lb, and the nil-lb placeholder on one's own row would require the row owner to have lost state — the restart/durability path (Durable false, replay unread) rather than a legal history of the modelled faults. The missing guard is retained as a real latent robustness gap and the reachability question is kept in remaining, along with the analogous ordering issue in handlePrepareReply (lb := inst.lb evaluated before its inst == nil check, epaxos/epaxos.go:1206-1210) and the still-unchecked A1 fast-path and A2 ballot/authority lines. Submitted action=explained for that candidate with feedback refs to the candidate, B-COMMIT, B-PHASE1, B-PREPARE-REPLY-LEADER and F-COMMITTED. Preflight validation returns valid=true; formal acceptance and any execution remain the controller's.
